hypotheses.statement: solang rejects the global builtin `ecrecover(hash,v,r,s)` at compile time as an unknown function, while solc accepts it; any contract using the ecrecover builtin fails to compile for pallet-contracts. This is a compile-time asymmetry, not a runtime semantic divergence.

evidence.note: solc compiled and ran the full contract including ecrecover; solang failed with 'unknown function or type ecrecover' at the ecrecover call site, so no runtime comparison of any builtin was possible.

hypotheses.next_probe: Remove the ecrecover call from CryptoProbe (keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 only) and rerun setData with args 0x010203; verify solang compiles and all three hashes plus packedHash/encodedHash match solc exactly.

hypotheses.statement: On solang/pallet-contracts, the ecrecover precompile at address 0x1 (if reachable via low-level call/delegatecall) may behave differently than EVM's ecrecover, since Substrate uses a different account/curve model; solang contracts may need `ecrecover` emulation via CryptoHasher-style host functions instead.

evidence.note: Could not test runtime ecrecover semantics because solang rejected the builtin; this motivates probing the raw 0x1 precompile path instead.

hypotheses.next_probe: Compile a contract that performs a static call to address 0x1 with a well-formed ecrecover input (known msg hash and signature from a fixed private key) and compare the returned 32-byte output against EVM's ecrecover result and against the signer address.
